pages.purpose: A catch-all 'body' page. From top to bottom it holds: a supplement checklist (Daily Stack), a water tracker plus a separate water-history card, steps (synced from the phone), 20-20-20 eye-break reminders, app-usage time, sleep, weight with a muscle/fat estimate and progress photos, body measurements, and a calorie ring that links to food.html. Below that sits a hidden Meal Prep tracker and an unreachable 'Fuel Coach' modal, both still in the file. Data syncs through the Supabase row uid:health (local mirror: localStorage dashboard:sync:health:v1). The page also reads the rows uid:steps, uid:screen, uid:food and uid:po-coach.
pages.screensOfScrollOnPhone: About 7-9 screens at 390x844 with the owner's 8 supplements. The Daily Stack card alone is over 2 screens: on phone each supplement row wraps to about 135px (the name, a 'Running low' button on its own line, and the x on another line), and the always-visible add form adds about 200px. Everything below it (water x2, steps, eyes, app usage, sleep, weight, measurements, food) is roughly another 4,500px.
pages.designNotes: Dark near-black background (#050506) with a faint drifting peach radial glow and a dot-grain overlay. Cards are translucent glass with blur. The screenshots (screenshot_health.png, ss_health.png) show the first screen almost entirely taken by labels and instructions instead of information: the section title 'DAILY STACK', a ticker reading 'STACK · <name> 5/8', the eyebrow 'DAILY STACK' again, then the headline 'Tap each as you take it'. The word 'stack' appears 3-4 times in 150px, and the biggest text on the page is an instruction. Every supplement row has a pulsing red border once its time window has passed (it animates forever), so the first thing the owner sees each day is three red 'you failed' boxes. That is a direct source of the 'duty' feeling. Rows are tall and clumsy on phone: the 'Running low' chip and the x button each drop to their own line. The x sits bottom-left like a stray control. The placeholder data ('XXXXX - Supplement of choice', 'how much MG, meal times, any data below') makes the screenshots look unfinished. At least four visual systems sit side by side. (1) The stack/water cards use mono uppercase eyebrows. (2) The sw-cards (steps/eyes/usage/sleep/measurements/food) use a '≡ SECTION' header. (3) The weight block keeps the gym page's mint palette (--good #6ee7b7) and a 'WEIGHT' divider rule ('keeps its original look' per a code comment). (4) The hidden fuel hero uses Georgia italic serif. Styling mixes var() tokens with many hard-coded inline colours (#f472b6, #f0a500, #e05252, #22c55e), so skins only partly apply. Emoji are used as icons (🌅🍽️🌙⏱️🥤🍶🧴⚙️🔔). Charts are inconsistent: inline SVG bars for water and steps, SVG paths for weight, a canvas bar chart for sleep history, and div bars for the measurements sparkline. Several cards show their configuration inline instead of results. The Eye Breaks card always shows a dimmed settings form (every / rest / from-to / chime) plus a long note about Roblox fullscreen and Windows Do-Not-Disturb, which is useless on an iPhone. The footer says '// editable template · all data stays in your browser', which is wrong (everything syncs to Supabase) and is leftover template text. What works: the steps ring with 7-day bars is clean and needs no input. The weight hero number with its 7-day-average line and soft glow is the most premium-looking element. The water quick-add buttons (Cup / Bottle / Big bottle) are good one-tap targets. There is no top-of-page summary: nothing says 'here is your body today' in one glance. You have to scroll through 10 cards and assemble it yourself.

features.name: Daily Stack: supplement checklist
features.whatItDoes: Lists the user's supplements grouped into Morning (7-10), Lunch (12-2), Evening (9-11) and Anytime windows. Tapping the circle marks one as taken. A progress bar shows 'x / N taken today · resets at 6 AM'. A day is counted as ending at 6 AM.
features.manualInputs: One tap per supplement per day. With the owner's 8 items that is 8 taps a day, spread over 3 time windows, so the app has to be opened and scrolled about 3 times a day. Supplements are added once each (see the add-form feature).
features.valueReturned: Adherence tracking (did I take X today?). It does not show a trend or history view, so past days' ticks are stored but never displayed on this page.
features.dataKeys: Synced in uid:health / _dbH: 'stack:items' (array of {id,name,dose,window,note,tag,ordered}), 'stack:taken:YYYY-MM-DD' ({itemId: timestamp}; one key per day, kept forever), 'stack:low' (array of ids). food.html also reads stack:items and stack:taken:* to show a supplement note.
features.overlapsWith: food.html's supplements group, which shows a note pointing back to Health. The ticker and missed-alert features below repeat the same information.
features.automationPotential: Taking pills can't be detected, but the friction can be cut a lot. Use one 'Took my morning stack' tap per window (3 taps a day, or 1 if most items are 'anytime') instead of one per item, and allow per-item exceptions on long-press. Remind through the existing push (api/cron-reminders.js) at window time instead of making the user open the page.

features.name: Stack ticker (rotating status banner)
features.whatItDoes: A banner at the top of the stack card. Every 5 seconds it cycles through messages such as '<item> — missed morning dose' and '<item> — running low, reorder soon', with a red or orange dot and an 'issues / total' count.
features.manualInputs: none
features.valueReturned: Restates what the red rows below already show. Its only distinct content is the reorder reminder.
features.dataKeys: Reads stack:items, stack:taken:<date> and stack:low.
features.overlapsWith: Missed-dose red rows; the Running-low chips.
features.automationPotential: Fold into a single status line on a home or body summary ('2 left this evening · reorder creatine'). Drop the rotating animation.

features.name: Missed-dose red pulse
features.whatItDoes: Once a window's cutoff hour passes, any unticked item in it gets a red border with a pulsing box-shadow animation that never stops.
features.manualInputs: none
features.valueReturned: Mostly guilt. It doesn't help the user catch up; it marks the item as failed. In both screenshots the first thing visible is three red pulsing boxes.
features.dataKeys: Computed from STACK_WINDOWS cutoffHour and stack:taken.
features.overlapsWith: Stack ticker.
features.automationPotential: Replace with a neutral 'not logged' state, plus one push reminder before the window closes.

features.name: Running-low flag
features.whatItDoes: A '↓ Running low' chip on each supplement. Toggling it marks the item for reorder and feeds the ticker.
features.manualInputs: One tap when a bottle gets low and one to clear it. A few times a month at most.
features.valueReturned: A reorder reminder. Useful but rare, and the chip takes a full line under every supplement on phone.
features.dataKeys: 'stack:low' (array of item ids) in uid:health.
features.overlapsWith: Stack ticker.
features.automationPotential: Could become 'pills left' with an auto-decrement on each tick and an alert at about 7 days left. At minimum, move it to long-press or edit mode.

features.name: Add to stack form + supplement autocomplete database
features.whatItDoes: An always-visible form (Name, Dose, Window dropdown, + Add). Typing a name searches a built-in database of about 70 supplements (creatine, D3, magnesium glycinate and others), each with a researched dose, best time window and timing note. Picking a match fills in the dose and window.
features.manualInputs: A one-time typing step per supplement. Picking a database match is about 3 taps; a custom item needs typing.
features.valueReturned: Saves looking up dose and timing. The notes are genuinely useful (for example 'Fat-soluble — take with biggest meal'). But the form sits permanently on the page and takes about 200px on phone, for something done a few times a year.
features.dataKeys: Writes 'stack:items'. The SUPPLEMENT_DB constant (about 11KB) is hard-coded in the page.
features.overlapsWith: none
features.automationPotential: The database already removes most typing. Put it behind an 'Edit stack' button or a sheet.

features.name: Inline edit / delete supplement
features.whatItDoes: Tapping a supplement's name or dose line turns it into editable text (contenteditable). The x deletes the item and its ticks immediately, with no confirmation.
features.manualInputs: Rare edits.
features.valueReturned: Editing in place. However, deletion fires on pointerdown with preventDefault and no confirm. On iPhone, a finger that starts a scroll on the x (which sits on its own line at the left edge of every row) deletes the supplement. This plausibly explains the 'supplements keep disappearing' problem mentioned in code comments.
features.dataKeys: stack:items, stack:taken:<date>, stack:low.
features.overlapsWith: none
features.automationPotential: Move to an edit mode with swipe-to-delete or a confirm step.

features.name: Water today card (quick-add)
features.whatItDoes: Shows ml drunk today against a computed target, a progress bar with a 'healthy zone' band, and three quick-add buttons (Cup 250ml / Bottle 500ml / Big 1L, editable sizes). Also has '− Undo last' and a pacing hint ('Behind pace — 1.2 L to go'). A setup notice appears until the profile is filled in. Logging gives +5 XP, capped.
features.manualInputs: One tap per drink, about 4-8 times a day.
features.valueReturned: A live hydration-vs-target number and a pacing nudge. Simple and quick to read.
features.dataKeys: 'po_water_v1' in uid:health and in localStorage: {logs:{'YYYY-MM-DD': ml}, hist:{date:[ml,...]} for undo, sizes:{cup,bottle,big}, unit, bottleMl, glassMl, weightUnit, profile:{weightKg,age,sex,activityHrsPerWeek}, caffeineMgPerDay, substances[], _mlV2, _setup, _ts}. Read by index, coach, food, gym, trends and topbar.
features.overlapsWith: The topbar water pill and its '+' button (on every page, linking to health.html#water). The water widget on the home page (index.html). Trends.
features.automationPotential: Logging can't be automated, but the topbar '+' already gives one-tap logging from anywhere. The page card could shrink to a ring inside a summary.

features.name: 'Why this target?' breakdown
features.whatItDoes: A collapsible panel itemising the water target: base (weight × 35ml), exercise, caffeine over 200mg, each substance, and a sex/age adjustment.
features.manualInputs: none (tap to expand)
features.valueReturned: Explains the number. Interesting once.
features.dataKeys: Computed from po_water_v1.profile, caffeineMgPerDay and substances.
features.overlapsWith: Water Settings.
features.automationPotential: n/a. It's already collapsed. Keep it collapsed.

features.name: Water Settings modal
features.whatItDoes: Opened from the gear icon. Fields: weight and unit, age, sex, training hours per week, cup/bottle/big-bottle sizes, average caffeine mg per day, and a 'Stimulants & meds' search (Adderall, nicotine pouches, alcohol, creatine and others, each adding ml per dose to the target). Also has a red 'Reset water data' button.
features.manualInputs: One-time: about 7 numeric fields, 2 segmented choices and an optional substance search with doses. Weight should in principle be re-entered as it changes.
features.valueReturned: A personalised target. But it duplicates body data the app already has elsewhere.
features.dataKeys: po_water_v1.profile, .sizes, .caffeineMgPerDay, .substances, .weightUnit, ._setup.
features.overlapsWith: The Fuel Coach profile (dashboard:mealPrep:v1:coach: sex/age/height/weight), the food.html profile in uid:food (heightCm/age/sex), onboarding, and the weight tracker (po_coach_weights). The same facts are typed in 3-4 places.
features.automationPotential: Take weight from the latest po_coach_weights entry. Derive training hours from gym logs (dashboard:gym:v1:logs sessions per week, already parsed on this page for the composition estimate). Take sex and age from one shared profile set at onboarding. After that, only cup sizes need setting.

features.name: Water history card (14-day sparkline + 6-day list)
features.whatItDoes: A separate card labelled 'LAST 14 DAYS' with an SVG bar chart against a target line, then a list of the previous 6 days with bars and ml.
features.manualInputs: none
features.valueReturned: Consistency over two weeks. The 6-day list repeats the same data as the sparkline above it.
features.dataKeys: po_water_v1.logs.
features.overlapsWith: The water card. trends.html also charts water.
features.automationPotential: Make it one compact 7-14-day strip inside the water card (or Trends), and remove the list.

features.name: Topbar water pill + '+' (cross-page, visible here)
features.whatItDoes: Injected by topbar.js on every page: a pill showing water progress that links to health.html#water, plus a '+' that logs one drink.
features.manualInputs: One tap per drink.
features.valueReturned: The lowest-friction water logging path in the app.
features.dataKeys: po_water_v1 (localStorage, plus _dbH on the health page). Polls uid:health every 4s.
features.overlapsWith: The water card's quick-add buttons.
features.automationPotential: Already one tap. But its 4-second poll downloads the whole uid:health row, including progress photos (see cross-cutting observations).

features.name: Steps card
features.whatItDoes: A ring showing today's steps against a goal, the 7-day average, best this week, and 7-day bars. The data comes from the phone through an iOS Shortcuts automation that calls /api/steps. Has an empty-state explainer.
features.manualInputs: None daily. A one-time setup of about 5 minutes (see Step sync setup).
features.valueReturned: Daily movement against a goal, plus a weekly trend, with no logging. The best effort-to-value ratio on the page.
features.dataKeys: Supabase row 'uid:steps': {token, goal, days:{'YYYY-MM-DD': steps}}, written by api/steps.js. The token is also used by app usage.
features.overlapsWith: none
features.automationPotential: Already automated. This pipeline (a Shortcut automation hitting /api/steps with a secret token) is the page's most valuable asset. It could also carry sleep, weight, resting HR and workouts from Apple Health.

features.name: Step sync setup modal + step goal
features.whatItDoes: Shows the personal /api/steps URL with a copy button, step-by-step iPhone (Shortcuts → Find Health Samples → Get Contents of URL) and Android (MacroDroid/Tasker) instructions, and a daily step-goal input.
features.manualInputs: One-time Shortcut building, about 6 steps. The goal is set once.
features.valueReturned: Enables automatic steps.
features.dataKeys: uid:steps.token, uid:steps.goal.
features.overlapsWith: The app usage setup modal, which uses the same token and a similar instructions UI.
features.automationPotential: Offer a prebuilt iCloud Shortcut link instead of manual building. Move to Settings.

features.name: Screen & Eyes: 20-20-20 eye breaks
features.whatItDoes: A toggle for a break timer that runs in topbar.js (window.dashEyes). Shows breaks today, a day streak, next break in X min, and 7-day bars. The settings are always visible: interval, rest seconds, active hours, chime, an enable-notifications button, a preview-break button and a long caveat note.
features.manualInputs: One-time configuration. On a computer, it only works while a dashboard tab stays open.
features.valueReturned: On iPhone, nothing: the card itself says it 'only runs on a computer'. On desktop, a break nudge plus counts. The owner uses the PWA on iPhone.
features.dataKeys: Config in localStorage 'dashboard:eyes:v1' and 'dashboard:eyes:nextAt'. Stats in Supabase row 'uid:screen'.days {'YYYY-MM-DD': {done}}.
features.overlapsWith: App Usage (shares the uid:screen row).
features.automationPotential: If kept, make it a desktop-only setting in settings.html with no card on the phone's health page.

features.name: App Usage tracking
features.whatItDoes: Shows minutes per tracked app today (bars), the number of opens, and a total. The data comes from two iOS Shortcuts automations per app (Is Opened / Is Closed) calling /api/usage. Has an empty-state explanation of why total Screen Time isn't available.
features.manualInputs: Per app, a one-time setup of two automations (about 10 steps). Each tracked app then launches slightly slower. Nothing daily.
features.valueReturned: Minutes spent in, say, TikTok today. Mildly interesting, with no history or trend view and no goal. It's also not really 'health'.
features.dataKeys: Supabase row 'uid:screen'.apps {'YYYY-MM-DD': {appName: {ms, opens}}}, written by api/usage.js. Uses the uid:steps token.
features.overlapsWith: The eye-breaks card, which shares the uid:screen row. Step sync setup uses the same token and setup pattern.
features.automationPotential: Already automatic after setup. If kept, show one line ('TikTok 47m today') in a summary and put setup in Settings. Otherwise cut.

features.name: Sleep tracker (manual)
features.whatItDoes: 7-day bars coloured by hours (green 7h or more, amber 6h or more, red below 6), the average hours per night, and a '+ Log sleep' modal where you type hours (saved against today's date).
features.manualInputs: Daily: tap '+ Log sleep', type the hours, tap Save (3 taps plus typing every morning, after scrolling about 5 screens down to find it).
features.valueReturned: A weekly sleep average and colour-coded nights.
features.dataKeys: 'dashboard:sleep:v1' in uid:health: {entries:[{date:'YYYY-MM-DD', hours}]}. The goal comes from settings sleepGoal (localStorage dashboard:settings:v1). Also read by coach, summary and trends.
features.overlapsWith: The sleep history chart (next feature), and trends.html.
features.automationPotential: High. iPhone already records sleep in Apple Health. Add a 'Sleep Analysis' sum to the existing daily step-sync Shortcut (for example an &sl= parameter on /api/steps) so manual entry drops to zero. Keep the manual entry as a fallback edit.

features.name: Sleep history canvas chart
features.whatItDoes: A 14-day canvas bar chart under the sleep bars, with a dashed goal line (settings sleepGoal, default 8h): green when the goal is met, red when under.
features.manualInputs: none
features.valueReturned: The same data as the 7-day bars just above, drawn a second time in a different chart style.
features.dataKeys: dashboard:sleep:v1; settings.sleepGoal.
features.overlapsWith: The sleep 7-day bars.
features.automationPotential: Make it a single chart.

features.name: Weight tracker
features.whatItDoes: A big latest-weight number, the change over the last 7 days, a day streak, and a 30-entry SVG line chart with a 7-day moving average and Y-axis. The input row is prefilled with the last weight; once today is logged it collapses to 'LOGGED TODAY ✓ / Edit'. Logging gives +25 XP a day.
features.manualInputs: Daily, or a few times a week: scroll to the card, tap the field, adjust the prefilled number, tap Save.
features.valueReturned: The trend (the 7-day average smooths out water noise) and the weekly change. This is the main input to the food targets in food.html. It is the best-looking card on the page.
features.dataKeys: 'po_coach_weights' in uid:health: [{dateKey:'YYYY-MM-DD', weight}], merged per entry on sync. Legacy 'dashboard:weight:v1' {entries:[{date,kg}]} and the migration flag 'dashboard:weightMoved:v1'. Read by index, food, gym (Strength Rank), coach, trends and topbar.
features.overlapsWith: The home page (index.html) weight display, trends.html, and the Water Settings weight field (duplicate entry).
features.automationPotential: If the owner has a smart scale, Apple Health can supply weight through the same Shortcut. Otherwise make it a one-tap quick log: a ± stepper on yesterday's value, available from home without scrolling. The 'streak' could go (it adds to the duty feeling).

features.name: Composition estimate (muscle vs fat)
features.whatItDoes: Combines the 30-day weight change with the strength trend, parsed from the gym page's raw set logs (Epley 1RM), to estimate how much of the change was muscle versus fat. Shows a headline ('mostly fat. Strength flat. Cut kcal.'), a muscle/fat bar and a footer of numbers.
features.manualInputs: None. It needs 2 or more weigh-ins and gym logs.
features.valueReturned: A speculative guess. yearsTraining is hard-coded to 1 (CONFIG_COMPOSITION), so the muscle-rate ceiling is always 0.45 kg/week. The verdicts are blunt and can be discouraging. It does turn data the app already has into something to act on.
features.dataKeys: Reads po_coach_weights, plus the Supabase row 'uid:po-coach'.data['dashboard:gym:v1:logs'] (a fetch on load and on every visibility change).
features.overlapsWith: Gym page strength analytics; the coach.
features.automationPotential: Already automatic. Show it as a one-line weekly insight at most, behind a tap.

features.name: Progress photos
features.whatItDoes: A 'PROGRESS PHOTOS → n photos · latest <date>' link opens a full-screen overlay with Take Photo (in-browser camera with flip, or the file-picker fallback) and From Library, plus a grid. The viewer has single and compare modes (side-by-side, with the weight change between the two photos, tap to cycle the comparison photo), and delete with confirmation.
features.manualInputs: Occasional, maybe weekly or monthly: open, shoot, done.
features.valueReturned: Visual progress, which is motivating and hard to get from numbers. Compare mode is nicely done.
features.dataKeys: 'po_coach_photos' in uid:health: [{id, dataUrl (base64 JPEG, compressed to max 1080px at quality 0.75), dateKey, weight}], merged by id on sync.
features.overlapsWith: Gym page (where it used to live).
features.automationPotential: Keep it manual, but move the image data out of the synced JSON row into Supabase Storage. Today every 4-5s poll on the health page re-downloads every photo (see cross-cutting observations).

features.name: Measurements
features.whatItDoes: A 2x2 grid of the latest Waist / Chest / L. Arm / R. Arm with the change from the previous entry, a waist sparkline of the last 5 entries, and a '+ Log measurements' modal (5 cm fields including optional hips, prefilled from the last entry).
features.manualInputs: Weekly or monthly: open the modal and type up to 5 numbers.
features.valueReturned: Body-shape change that the scale misses (the waist especially). Low frequency, but it takes a full card every visit.
features.dataKeys: 'dashboard:measurements:v1' in uid:health and localStorage: {entries:[{date, waist, chest, leftArm, rightArm, hips}]}. Only health.html uses it.
features.overlapsWith: Weight tracker (both are body composition).
features.automationPotential: No automatic source. Reduce to waist only, shown as a line under weight, with a monthly push prompt instead of a permanent card.

features.name: Food summary ring
features.whatItDoes: Reads today's entries from the Food page's uid:food row and shows a calorie ring, 'n items logged today', and protein grams. The whole card links to food.html. It refreshes every 60s and on focus.
features.manualInputs: none here (logging happens on food.html)
features.valueReturned: A glance at calories and protein. Bug: when no custom kcal goal is set, the fallback goal reads `ws[ws.length-1].kg`, but po_coach_weights entries store `.weight`. The goal then comes out as NaN and the ring never fills.
features.dataKeys: Reads Supabase row 'uid:food': days[date].entries[].n.kcal / protein_g, profile, custom.kcal. Reads po_coach_weights.
features.overlapsWith: food.html; the home page's meal and food widgets.
features.automationPotential: Already automatic. It belongs in a home or today summary rather than the health page.

features.name: Daily Meal Prep tracker (HIDDEN / dead)
features.whatItDoes: A meal checklist from a template (tick meals as eaten), a 'Today's fuel' hero (kcal left, macro bars, status pill), quick-add chips (an empty list), a 'Bulking adjustment guide' collapsible, Reset today, and modals for Log Meal, Manage Meals, Macro Targets and Edit Meal Template. The section is set to display:none ('absorbed into food.html v2.6.9'), but its HTML, about 16.8KB of JS and the mp-/fuel CSS still load and run.
features.manualInputs: none (invisible)
features.valueReturned: Nothing visible. It is dead weight in the page. The 'Reset all data' handler also clears localStorage keys while the data actually lives in _dbH, so it would do nothing anyway.
features.dataKeys: 'dashboard:mealPrep:v1:template' (array of meals {id,name,foods,kcal,protein,carbs,fat,notes}), 'dashboard:mealPrep:v1:daily' ({date:{mealId:{eaten,eatenAt,kcal,protein,carbs,fat,time,notes}, _extras:[]}}), 'dashboard:mealPrep:v1:settings' ({kcal/protein/carbs/fat:{min,max}}). All synced in uid:health and still read by index.html, coach.html, summary.html and food.html. Keep the data and remove the code.
features.overlapsWith: food.html, which replaced it.
features.automationPotential: n/a

features.name: Fuel Coach modal (UNREACHABLE)
features.whatItDoes: A two-step modal. Step 1 takes sex, age, height, weight, activity level and goal (cut/maintain/lean bulk/bulk). Step 2 gives BMR to TDEE to target kcal and macros, an auto-generated example meal day from a small food library ('Shuffle meals'), and a 'self-training check-in' that estimates actual daily burn from 14 days of weigh-ins plus logged meals. It also has an embedded AI chat (/api/coach) and buttons to apply the targets or the plan to Meal Prep. Its only opener (#mpCoachBtn) is inside the hidden meal-prep section, so it can't be reached. About 28KB of HTML, CSS and JS.
features.manualInputs: none (unreachable)
features.valueReturned: Nothing at present. The check-in idea (measured TDEE from weight trend and intake, then auto-adjusted calories) is the smartest 'save me thinking' logic on the page and is worth keeping in food.html or the coach. askCoach also references SUPABASE_URL out of scope, so the auth token is always empty.
features.dataKeys: 'dashboard:mealPrep:v1:coach' ({sex,age,height,weight,act,goal}, synced and read by coach.html). Writes mealPrep settings and template.
features.overlapsWith: coach.html (AI chat), food.html targets, the Water Settings profile.
features.automationPotential: Move the measured-TDEE check-in into food.html so it runs automatically each week from data the app already has. No form needed.

crossCuttingObservations:
health.html carries 10 visible cards, 1 hidden section and about 10 modals. On a phone, getting through all of it takes about 7-9 screens of scrolling, and there is no summary at the top. The owner has to scroll to find each input, which matches the complaint about having to "scroll and find".

DAILY CHORE TALLY (this page alone, as built):
- Supplements: about 8 taps across 3 separate visits.
- Water: 4-8 taps.
- Weight: about 3 taps plus an edit.
- Sleep: 3 taps plus typing.
- Total: roughly 20 interactions a day, plus weekly measurements and a one-time setup of 7+ fields for water. The setup for steps and app usage is also long (building Shortcuts by hand).

THE STRONGEST ASSET IS UNDERUSED: the Shortcuts → /api/steps token pipeline already makes steps zero-effort. Extending the same daily automation to Apple Health's Sleep Analysis (and weight, if a smart scale exists) removes the two most annoying manual inputs.

DUPLICATED DATA ENTRY:
- Weight, sex and age are typed into Water Settings (po_water_v1.profile), the Fuel Coach (mealPrep:v1:coach), the food.html profile (uid:food.profile), and onboarding.
- Weight is also logged in the weight tracker.
- Training hours are typed even though gym logs exist.
- One shared profile would remove all of these.

DUPLICATED DISPLAYS:
- Water: the topbar pill, the water card, the 14-day sparkline, the 6-day list, the home page and Trends.
- Sleep: 7-day bars and a 14-day canvas chart on the same card.
- Weight: here, on home and on Trends.
- AI chat: Fuel Coach and coach.html.
- Food: the ring here and food.html.

GUILT MECHANICS THAT MAKE IT FEEL LIKE A DUTY:
- Missed supplements pulse red forever.
- A ticker cycles "missed dose" messages every 5s.
- Streak counters for weight and eye breaks.
- XP pop-ups for water (+5), weight (+25) and meals (+8).
- The blunt composition verdict ("mostly fat... Cut kcal").
- Headlines are instructions ("Tap each as you take it") rather than information.

DEAD OR WRONG CODE (a redesign can delete it):
- About 57KB (about 21% of the file) is unreachable: the hidden Meal Prep section, its 4 modals and 16.8KB script, plus the Fuel Coach CSS, modal and 20KB script.
- window.renderWeightChart draws to a #weightChart canvas that doesn't exist.
- Unused .water-embed/.water-iframe CSS.
- The footer "all data stays in your browser" is false.
- The mpResetAll button clears localStorage, but the data lives in _dbH.

BUGS FOUND (from source, not yet confirmed in the live app):
1. Supplement × deletes on pointerdown with no confirm. On iPhone, the × sits on its own line at the left edge of each row, so touching it to start a scroll can silently delete a supplement. This likely explains the "supplements keep disappearing" comment in the sync code.
2. The food ring's fallback goal reads `.kg` on po_coach_weights entries, which store `.weight`. The ring stays empty unless a custom kcal goal is set.
3. The step-sync tab handler selects every `.sy-tab`, including the App Usage modal's tabs. Clicking an app-usage tab also flips the step-sync panes.
4. The Fuel Coach's askCoach references SUPABASE_URL out of scope, so its token is always empty.

PERFORMANCE / EFFICIENCY:
- The page polls Supabase constantly: the health sync every 5s, the topbar water pull every 4s, and steps, usage and the food ring every 60s. The eye card re-renders every 30s, and the gym logs are fetched again on every focus.
- The 5s and 4s polls each download the entire uid:health row. That row embeds every progress photo as base64 (about 100-200KB each) plus one stack:taken:<date> key per day, kept forever.
- On a phone this costs speed, data and battery. Photos should move to Supabase Storage, and the polling should be reduced to on-focus plus a single interval.
